description: The 2023 list of the most critical API risks, led by broken object level authorization.
Copying the request body straight into a model update, so clients can set fields like `role` or `ownerId`.
Responses that return whole rows (hashes, internal flags) and rely on the frontend to hide fields.
Server-side request forgery: the server fetches an attacker-chosen URL, reaching internal services or cloud metadata.
A browser policy on which origins may read responses. It is not authentication and does not protect against non-browser clients.
Each service, key and database user gets only the permissions it needs, limiting the damage of a leak.
